review_candidates.title: Moon Base Program: Senior Electronics Engineer
review_candidates.description: Build the brains that will run a factory on the Moon. GRU Space’s Moon Base Program is developing a robotic factory designed to manufacture humanity’s first bricks on the lunar surface. You’ll own the avionics and embedded software that power the payload, control its mechanisms, run the manufacturing process, and report what happened. You’ll take the system from prototype instrumentation through flight hardware, integrated testing, and delivery for lunar lander integration. This is a full-time, in-person role in Hawthorne, Los Angeles . You’ll work closely with the people designing the mechanisms and developing the material process. When a sensor disagrees with a test result or a mechanism stalls, you’ll help trace the problem from the bench through the firmware—and turn the fix into a system we can trust. What You’ll Do Own the avionics architecture: computing, power distribution and conditioning, sensors, actuator interfaces, harnessing, grounding, and electrical protection. Design and bring up controller boards and mixed-signal electronics. Evaluate purchased modules and make practical build-versus-buy decisions with the payload lead. Write embedded C/C++ for payload sequencing, closed-loop control, data logging, watchdogs, and fault detection and recovery. Own the payload’s electrical and data interfaces with the lunar lander, including interface control documents (ICDs), command definitions, telemetry, and interface verification. Design and integrate harnesses for the payload’s mechanisms and sensors, accounting for routing, shielding, strain relief, and environmental requirements. Build hardware-in-the-loop tests and inject faults: power interruptions, sensor failures, stalled mechanisms, communications loss, and resets. Assess component suitability for the mission’s thermal and radiation environments, working with specialists where needed. Maintain flight software releases, test evidence, and as-built documentation. Develop ground tools for integration, mission rehearsals, and lunar operations. What We’re Looking For You’ve personally been the RE for a flight avionics system or substantial spacecraft electronics subsystem from concept, testing, integration, and launch. Full-cycle PCB experience: schematic, layout, fabrication, bring-up, and in-system debugging. Embedded C/C++ experience controlling physical hardware, including state machines, watchdogs, and fault handling. Practical power electronics experience, including conditioning, protection, actuator drivers, and power budgets. Experience defining and debugging serial interfaces such as RS-485, including framing, error detection, and recovery. Strong bench skills: you can trace a fault across a board, harness, sensor, and firmware using an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, and debugger. Familiarity with spacecraft wiring, grounding, shielding, and electromagnetic compatibility. Clear technical communication and the ability to work closely with mechanical, materials, and thermal engineers. Experience with lunar payloads, radiation-tolerant electronics, motor and valve controls, onboard storage, and mission operations is especially relevant. How To Apply Share evidence of excellence and technical work you’re most proud of. Describe the hardware and software you personally owned, a difficult failure you resolved, and the tests that showed your system was ready to fly. Tell us why you want your life’s work to be on the Moon. If you want to build the systems that help humanity establish a permanent presence beyond Earth, we’d like to hear from you. ITAR Requirements To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. About GRU Space GRU Space is building America’s Moon Base. Brick by brick. We’re doing this via in-situ resource utilization: by building factories that convert lunar regolith into structural materials so we can construct with what’s on the Moon instead of shipping everything from Earth. This will be the most consequential technology unlock of our time: when humanity cracks the problem of manufacturing the first product on the Moon, we’re ushering in a brand new technology tree.
